items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: and I’m sitting there with the guy. I don’t know him, I don’t know anything about him, I just know that I saw you in my dream

ctx.x: he was leading a drum circle, whether he had a gig that night at the club, etcetera. I was attached to Emile’s drums. Drum in tow and we went. And I left there a month later after I had had a vision and a dream that there was this entire, this entire lineage of drummers that I was supposed to come into contact with on my path. And I saw them all, Monk, I saw every single one of them in the dream, who I would have to connect with. And I told Emile, I got up and I told Emile about the dream. And Emile said,…

move. Don’t move.” And tears are running down my face. And I said, “It’s you! It’s you, it’s you.” And I’m talking. “You, I saw you in my dream. I saw you in my dream, I saw you.” And it was Montego Joe you know? Montego was one of those classic Caribbean percussionists, man, who had made it sort of on the big stage with guys like Babatunde Olatunji and, you know, Chief Bey, and you know, I mean it was that era, like the 50s, 60s, etcetera, and Montego was one of those musicians who had played, you know as a…
How did he react to that?
